questions.text:
Rātā Dog Grooming is a mobile grooming service owned by Sam. Every year, Sam provides each of her three staff members with a branded apron and tool kit costing $150 per set. Total cost: $450.

Justify why the aprons and tool kits are reported as an expense. In your answer, explain the three characteristics of the expense definition and the recognition criteria of faithful representation.
questions.expectedAnswer: Expense characteristics: (1) decrease in economic benefits (cash outflow of $450), (2) during the reporting period, (3) results in a decrease in equity other than owner withdrawals. Faithful representation: the expense accurately reflects the cost incurred for staff equipment, is complete, neutral, and free from error.
questions.markingGuide: A: Identifies expense characteristics. M: Explains all three with context. E: Links to faithful representation.

questions.text:
Statement of Accounting Policies: Inventory is reported at the lower of cost or net realisable value.

A flood damaged grooming products stored in the van. Products originally costing $6,500 now have a net realisable value of $1,800. Total inventory at historical cost is $28,000.

Justify how inventory should be reported in the Statement of Financial Position. Explain the qualitative characteristic of relevance and one limitation.
questions.expectedAnswer: Inventory reported at $23,300 ($28,000 - $6,500 + $1,800). The damaged stock is written down from $6,500 to $1,800 (lower of cost or NRV). Relevance: reporting at NRV provides users with more relevant information about the true value of inventory. Limitation: NRV is an estimate that may not reflect the actual selling price achieved.
questions.markingGuide: A: Calculates correct inventory value. M: Explains relevance and applies lower of cost/NRV. E: Discusses limitation.

questions.text:
In February, Sam purchased a new grooming van for $35,000 cash and signed a new 4-year vehicle lease agreement.

Explain how the new grooming van and lease illustrate the concept of going concern.
questions.expectedAnswer: Going concern assumes the entity will continue operating into the foreseeable future. Purchasing a $35,000 van and signing a 4-year lease demonstrate Sam's intention and expectation that the business will continue operating for at least 4 years. Without this assumption, assets would need to be reported at liquidation value rather than historical cost.
questions.markingGuide: A: Defines going concern. M: Links van purchase and lease to continued operation. E: Explains implications for financial reporting.

questions.text: Justify, using the characteristics/definition of an asset, how the grooming van will be reported in the Statement of Financial Position.
questions.expectedAnswer: Grooming van reported as non-current asset (PPE) at $35,000. Asset characteristics: (1) controlled by the entity (owned), (2) as a result of a past event (purchased in February), (3) from which future economic benefits are expected (used to generate grooming income over several years).
questions.markingGuide: A: Identifies as non-current asset. M: Explains asset characteristics with context. E: Links all three characteristics and justifies amount.

questions.text:
The grooming van is depreciated using the diminishing value method at 25% per annum. The grooming equipment inside the van is depreciated at $1,500 per year using the straight line method.

Justify how Rātā Dog Grooming depreciates its assets. Explain the definition of depreciation and why different methods are appropriate for different assets.
questions.expectedAnswer: Depreciation: systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over its useful life. Diminishing value is appropriate for the van because vehicles lose more value in early years due to rapid wear and technological change. Straight line is appropriate for grooming equipment because it provides roughly equal benefit each year. Different methods match the pattern of economic benefit consumption.
questions.markingGuide: A: Defines depreciation. M: Explains both methods. E: Justifies why each method is appropriate for each asset.

questions.text:
RĀTĀ DOG GROOMING — BOOK NOW: Premium dog grooming $85/session. Pay a 50% deposit to secure your booking.

By 31 March 2025, Sam had received deposits totalling $4,250 for upcoming grooming appointments. The grooming will be completed and the balance paid in April and May 2025.

Using the accrual basis concept, justify the treatment and reporting of these deposits. Explain the impact on the Income Statement and the Statement of Financial Position.
questions.expectedAnswer: Accrual basis: transactions recorded when earned, not when cash received. The $4,250 deposits are not revenue yet because the grooming service hasn't been provided. Income Statement: no revenue recognised for these deposits. SFP: reported as a current liability (income in advance) because Sam has an obligation to either provide the service or refund the deposit.
questions.markingGuide: A: Identifies deposits not as revenue. M: Explains accrual basis and correct SFP treatment. E: Fully justifies classification as current liability.

questions.text:
Sam has received a monthly revenue summary for the quarter ended 31 August 2025.

| | June $ | July $ | August $ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grooming revenue | 14,000 | 11,500 | 15,500 |
| Retail product sales | 3,500 | 2,800 | 4,200 |
| Total revenue | 17,500 | 14,300 | 19,700 |

Discuss how separating the two types of revenue helps Sam's decision-making. Explain the qualitative characteristic of materiality.
questions.expectedAnswer: Materiality: information is material if omitting/misstating it could influence decisions. The separation reveals that both grooming and retail dipped in July (likely winter slowdown) but retail recovered strongly in August. If reported as one total, Sam might not see the different recovery patterns. This helps Sam plan staffing and stock purchases — e.g., ordering more retail products for the spring uptick.
questions.markingGuide: A: Defines materiality. M: Identifies seasonal patterns. E: Discusses how separation aids decision-making about business strategy.
